text:
The Blues have won four in a row, and none of them were quiet. A 9-6 win over New Jersey on Saturday came the night before a shootout win over Edmonton, and over the four games St. Louis outscored teams 27-18 on just 14.9 expected goals. The chances were an even split, 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against), so finishing did the heavy lifting.

The goaltending story is the other thread. Joel Hofer has the hot hand: 4-1-0 over his last five starts with 4.0 goals saved above expected, and he got the start Sunday. Jordan Binnington, whose name has come up in trade talk, has stopped .844 over his last five starts, 3.9 goals worse than expected.

Logan Mailloux has 8 points in 7 games against 3.4 expected, and Jimmy Snuggerud scored on the power play in his 100th NHL game. The Robert Thomas line with Dylan Holloway and Snuggerud has played the most minutes together, at 52% of the expected goals.

At 13-9-2 the Blues sit 2.9 points above what their play has earned, and our race model calls them a coin flip for the playoffs at 47%. What to watch: whether Hofer keeps the net once the scoring settles back toward the chances.
headline: Blues win four straight on finishing and Hofer
